instructions.content: Read the existing rules file first and check every ### Rule: heading to avoid duplicates before appending anything.
If a rule with the same directive already exists, inform the user and do NOT create a duplicate.
Every rule entry MUST include a Rule title, a Directive (ALWAYS/NEVER phrasing preferred), and a Rationale.

PREFER scripts/validate-rules.sh generate over hand-typing the three-line rule block, and run scripts/validate-rules.sh validate to confirm the file still has valid structure before treating the change as done.
Only invoke this skill when the user explicitly requests a new rule -- do not infer rule creation from unrelated conversation.
NEVER add a rule without reading the existing rules file first -- blind appending creates duplicate or conflicting directives.
NEVER accept a vague user instruction as the rule body -- every rule must have a precise ALWAYS/NEVER directive and a rationale.
NEVER create a rule for memory or ephemeral notes -- route those to vault-capture or a context finding instead.
Do not use rules-management for instructions that belong in the project's own agent-facing docs (repo map, workflow, tool conventions), or for personal preferences that don't affect agent behaviour.
PREFER merging related rules into a single entry TYPICALLY over scattering them across multiple entries.
If the user asks for a rule that overlaps with an existing one, suggest amending rather than duplicating.
Rules should be few and high-signal -- avoid documenting the obvious.
